PR 1814 at exact head 7b42135b379f7b8b166ffadab641b2739036bf54 (merge of Ports candidate 3ee3b345 with actual Vault main 068da01e) represents a well-formed security improvement. The core changes are: (1) replacement of the non-atomic `writeFileSync` + `chmodSync` port-file write in the JS sidecar with an atomic exclusive-create / `fchmodSync` / `renameSync` sequence exported as `publishSidecarPort`, with injected-filesystem support for failure tests; (2) elimination of the `Unconfirmed(DEFAULT_LOCAL_API_PORT)` fallback in `sidecar_publication.rs`, replaced by `AwaitingConfirmation` which leaves the port `None` on timeout rather than publishing a default that may belong to a foreign process; (3) a fail-closed `stale_port_cleanup` that stops startup on any unexpected error removing the previous port file, preventing an old publication from being mistaken for the new child; (4) gating `copy_diagnostics` on `confirmed_sidecar_target` so no HTTP request is constructed before confirmation; and (5) a renderer `warn` tone while `portConfirmed` is false or `port` is null. The workflow addition (`npm run test:port-publication` after `test:sidecar-ci`, before `build`) is additive only; existing action pins, permissions, event/fork conditions, and time limits are unchanged. The `package.json` script addition introduces no dependency, lockfile, install-script, or bin-entry change. All 15 changed paths are covered by comprehensive behavioral tests (22+6 inner green stages) and 10 independently mutation-tested controls on the prior head. The `targeted-tests-overrides.json` changes are additive for `test:port-publication` with preserved domain-retirement and release-capabilities entries. The bundle measures 469,980 bytes gzip against the unchanged 471,040-byte cap. No blocking findings were identified. One nonblocking finding is carried forward unchanged from the first review: the XMPP-bundle backup directory created inside the repository working tree during `test:sidecar-supervisor` native execution is not covered by any `.gitignore` rule, leaving a residual accidental-staging risk if cleanup fails with a prior bundle present.
